subject: Comp band specs + offer authorization: workstream and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Comp Band Working Group <comp-band@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Comp band specs + offer authorization: workstream and next steps

Team,

I pulled the latest benchmarking and baked it into a V3 comp band draft (attached). Key context: CompBench ran market medians across the AI infra / platform market (US West / East aggregated) and we added a set of geo anchors for EU/APAC projected next quarter. The goals for this thread:

- Agree on a clean definition for each level (IC L1-L6, Mgr L2-L4) we hand to recruiting.
- Finalize geo multipliers we use for offer guidance (anchoring vs market).
- Confirm offer approval gates (authorization levels for hiring managers, L4/L5 + GC signoff?).

Ask: Please review comp-band-draft-v3.xlsx and the geo-anchor reference PDF, comment inline in Drive by Friday EOD PDT. I’ve sketched suggested manager/PeopleOps approval thresholds in the sheet — these are intentionally conservative to start.

Immediate notes in the sheet:
- V3 moves Senior IC (L4) midpoint up 6% vs V2 based on Q2 comp inflation observed in San Francisco.
- We propose an explicit ‘above-market’ approval flow for any offer > 10% above midpoint (requires VP + People Lead signoff).

If nobody objects, I’ll route the doc to CompBench (external) for a quick reconciliation of their peer set and then send an internal summary to leadership next week.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Talent Partners (Hiring Operations)
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: comp-band-draft-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), geo-anchor-reference.pdf (report)

Subject: Re: Comp band specs + offer authorization: workstream and next steps

Ben — thanks for pulling this together. Quick read-through notes: 

1) Level definitions: please separate out scope (impact/scope vs IC vs manager) into a short rubric column — makes calibration calls much faster.

2) Approval gates: the >10% threshold is fine but recommend we specify token budget authority for hiring managers vs directors (e.g., up to 3% above midpoint without HC lead). Otherwise we’ll get escalations for every Sr IC hire.

3) Geo multipliers: the PDF shows APAC as +8% to US mid; that feels high for SG and AU — ask CompBench to break APAC into SG/AU/IN.

I’ll join a sync if you want to run a 30-min calibration with Recruiting + two hiring managers on Thursday.

— Vivek
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: CompBench: revised peer set + APAC split requested

Hi Ben / team —

Thanks for sharing the draft. We ran the updated peer set across our US/EU/APAC buckets and attached a short reconciliation. Highlights we observed:

- For L4 (Senior IC) and L5 (Staff IC), open market premium in SF is ~7% vs aggregated US tech mid.
- APAC: SG and AU are indeed closer to US-equivalent ranges for senior technical ICs; India (Bengaluru/Hyderabad) is ~35-45% below US mid depending on role complexity.
- We recommend splitting APAC into: Australia / Singapore (anchor +2% to US mid) and India (anchor -38% to US mid).

We’ve uploaded a short PDF that maps suggested band midpoints and 25/75 percentiles for each market. If you want, we can prepare a one-page summary for Recruiting to use in offer training.

Attached: compbench-recon-20260722.pdf

Best,
Sara Lim

Agree with Vivek and CompBench — split APAC into AU/SG and IN in the public guidance. A couple of governance asks:

- Include a short FAQ page for hiring managers on how to handle counteroffers and internal parity checks.
- For offers that exceed the VP signoff threshold, require a 1-line rationale in the approval ticket (not a long doc).

Ben — please add a column in the sheet with the proposed manager-level token (percent over midpoint allowed without escalation) and an example approval flow for L4 vs L5. I’ll review that version on Friday morning.

Subject: Re: Comp band specs + offer authorization: workstream and next steps

Ben/Team — quick operational question from Recruiting: when Recruiting pulls an offer authorization, which value do we populate in Workday — midpoint, target (midpoint +/- geo), or suggested offer? We need a single canonical field to drive approval automation.

Suggested: use 'suggested offer' (rounded to nearest $500) as the value that auto-populates and triggers the approval flow. Also recommend a flag field for 'above-market-justification' (text up to 250 chars) if the suggested offer is >10% above midpoint.

If everyone agrees, I’ll update the Workday flow and the Recruiting playbook with these field names.

— Neha
Sr. Manager, Recruiting Operations

Thanks all — good alignment. Recap + next steps: 

1) CompBench will split the APAC bucket into AU/SG and IN; they’ll send a 1-pager by Monday (Sara copied).
2) I’ll add the manager token column to comp-band-draft-v3.xlsx: proposed default = up to 3% for hiring manager, 3-10% for Director, >10% requires VP + People Lead signoff + 1-line rationale in approval ticket.
3) Neha will: change Workday to store 'suggested_offer' as the canonical approval field and add the 'above_market_justification' text flag.
4) Monica & Recruiting: prepare a 20-min training for hiring managers on the new flow (offer prep + examples) to run next Wednesday.

Action owners: CompBench (Sara) / Ben / Neha / Monica. I’ll push the updated sheet to Drive and share the leadership summary no later than Tuesday morning.

If no objections, I’ll mark this thread as the official working document and start the Headcount approval ticket flow for the two pending Senior IC reqs (WD-4821, WD-4822).

Ben
